memberdef.name: computePhysicsKernels

briefdescription.para: Computes the physics kernels (internal forces and their derivatives) for the particle.

detaileddescription.para:
Updates the center kinematics from the main domain (the center displacement is incremented by $ \sum_B N_B \Delta\boldsymbol{q}_B $ and $ \Delta\boldsymbol{F}_c $ is set, see the class documentation), then calls computePhysicsKernelsOnSubdomains(). As for all Marmot entities, the state variables are updated in place, and the host restores them to the last accepted state before each evaluation (EdelweissMeshfree does so in every computePhysicsKernels call): the center displacement thus stays the total one, which acceptStateAndPosition() applies to the undeformed domain.
dQ
Incremental nodal displacements (the first nDim dofs of each node are used).
fInt
Internal force vector.
dFInt_ddQ
Stiffness matrix (derivative of internal forces with respect to incremental displacements).
timeNew
The current simulation time.
dT
The time step size.

briefdescription.para: Computes the smoothed derivatives of shape functions for a particle domain.

detaileddescription.para:
This method uses a boundary integral approach (SNNI/SCNI) over the smoothing domain to compute the derivatives of the shape functions, with one point per face, $ \partial N_A / \partial Y_i = \frac{1}{|\Omega_s|}\sum_f N_A(\boldsymbol{Y}_f)\, n_{f,i}\,dA_f $, where $ \boldsymbol{Y}_f $ is the face center and $ \boldsymbol{n}_f\,dA_f $ the boundary surface vector of the smoothing domain and $ |\Omega_s| $ its volume.
particleDomain
The particle domain for which to compute smoothed derivatives.
An Eigen::MatrixXd containing the smoothed derivatives of shape functions (dN_dY).

briefdescription.para: Sets the VCI order and updates the number of VCI constraints.

detaileddescription.para:
The number of constraints is $ \binom{k + n_{\text{dim}}}{n_{\text{dim}}} $ for the order $ k $. Unlike GenericParticle::setVCIOrder(), the basis is not evaluated here but in assignMeshfreeKernelFunctions() (per subdomain), which must therefore be called after the order has been set.

The desired VCI order.

briefdescription.para: A generic, physics-independent base class for particles with subdomain integration (SDI).

detaileddescription.para: The particle domain (a ParticleDomain, e.g., a quadrilateral or a hexahedron) is uniformly subdivided once into $ 2^{n_{\text{dim}}} $ subdomains (ParticleDomain::uniformSubdivided()). Each subdomain $ s $ is an integration point of its own: the derived class attaches a material point to it and integrates the weak form as a sum over the subdomains. The shape functions of a subdomain are evaluated at its center, and their gradients are smoothed over its smoothing domain $ \Omega_s $ by the divergence theorem, with one point (the face center $ \boldsymbol{Y}_f $) per face $ f $ and the boundary surface vector $ \boldsymbol{n}_f\,dA_f $, \[ \frac{\partial N_A}{\partial Y_i}\bigg|_s \approx \frac{1}{|\Omega_s|} \sum_f N_A(\boldsymbol{Y}_f)\, n_{f,i}\, dA_f \] (see _smoothDerivativeShapeFunctionsForParticleDomain()). The test functions start as copies of the trial functions and are changed only by the VCI correction.

The particle as a whole moves with its center: in computePhysicsKernels(), the displacement increment and the deformation gradient increment of the center are computed from the shape functions of the main domain, \[ \Delta\boldsymbol{u}_c = \sum_B N_B\, \Delta\boldsymbol{q}_B, \qquad \Delta\boldsymbol{F}_c = \boldsymbol{I} + \sum_B \Delta\boldsymbol{q}_B \otimes \frac{\partial N_B}{\partial \boldsymbol{Y}}, \] and in acceptStateAndPosition() the total central deformation gradient $ \boldsymbol{F}_c \leftarrow \Delta\boldsymbol{F}_c\, \boldsymbol{F}_c $ and the total center displacement $ \boldsymbol{u}_c $ move the main domain and all subdomains (ParticleDomain::acceptStateAndPosition()).
